head: pr17394-r16
report:
Writing both probes.

Two defects need fixing before merge. I reproduced both by running the changed code. A third is still a hypothesis.

## 1. `omp worktree clear` deletes the directory a symlink points to, even outside the worktrees dir

**Mechanism.** The scan checks each entry with `fs.stat` (`worktree-cli.ts:320`, `classifyDir` at `:358`). `fs.stat` follows symlinks, so a symlink whose target contains an `m/` dir or a marker is classified as `task-isolation` (T1). At deletion (`worktree-cli.ts` clear loop, diff lines 72–80), the patch resolves the path again with `resolveSandboxIdentity(target.path)`, which calls `realpath` (T2). It then runs `stopRetainedMount` and `fs.rm(sandbox, {recursive:true})` on the **resolved target**, not on the entry it scanned.

The comment above that code says the resolve is there to defend against a symlink swapped in between scan and delete. It does the reverse: before this patch, `fs.rm(target.path)` removed only the link. Now the removal follows the link to wherever it points.
- With `--all`, nothing is checked under the lock, so any target is deleted.
- Without `--all`, a target whose marker says `retired` is deleted, even when it is outside `getWorktreesDir()`.

**Trigger.** Create `~/.omp/wt/tlink0001 -> ~/project` (any directory with an `m/` subdir), then run `omp worktree clear --all`. `~/project` is deleted and the link is left dangling.

**Measured** (`clear-symlink.test.ts` in the scratch dir):
```
result: {"removed":1,"failed":0}
link still exists: false (lstat) true
victim outside worktrees dir still exists: false
precious.txt exists: false
[no --all] link lstat exists: true
[no --all] victim exists: false
```
Control, the old deletion call (`borrow-cwd.test.ts`, first test):
```
old path: target survives fs.rm(link): true
```

**Fix direction.** Keep the fact the scan established. `lstat` the entry under the lock and refuse or unlink when it is a symlink. If you keep the realpath, check that it is still inside `getWorktreesDir()` before deleting.

## 2. The eval-tool kernel borrow holds one kernel while the tool calls go to another

**Mechanism.** `borrowEvalToolKernels` (`task/eval-tools.ts:154–165`, called from `eval/agent-bridge.ts`) resolves the kernel identity once, at borrow time (T1): `resolvePythonKernelIdentity(session)` reads `session.cwd` then. Every later tool call made by the kept-alive subagent resolves it again from the live session (`eval-tools.ts:184–188`, T2). The borrow exists for one case, stated in its docstring: "the owner's next cell in another directory reclaims it mid-run". In exactly that case `session.cwd` has moved:
- The borrow pins the old kernel at cwd A until the subagent's lifecycle ends.
- The subagent's tool calls go to the kernel at cwd B, which does not have the `@tool` definitions, or is not running at all.

So the protection guards a kernel nobody calls, and the old kernel (heap included) leaks until the subagent is released. The descriptors themselves came from an earlier `describeEvalTools` await, which is a third lookup through the same moving handle.

**Trigger.** In a parent eval cell at cwd A, define `@tool t`, then spawn an eval agent with `tools=["t"]` (the agent is kept alive). Next, `cd` to B and run a cell there. When the child calls `t`, the call goes to B's kernel.

**Measured** (`borrow-cwd.test.ts`; only the Python executor's I/O is stubbed, the `eval-tools.ts` logic is the real code):
```
borrowed kernel cwd: [ "/work/a" ]  tool call kernel cwd: [ "/work/b" ]
```
I did not check the JS side. `borrowVmContext(resolveJsKernelIdentity(session).sessionKey)` has the same shape and needs the same fix.

**Fix direction.** Resolve the identity once, when the tools are described. Pass that identity to `createEvalCustomTools` and to the borrow, so the calls and the hold name the same kernel.

## 3. (Hypothesis, not measured) `markUnfinishedWriter` can recreate a sandbox dir the teardown already retired

`isolation-lease.ts:266–274`: `findSandboxBase(cwd)` finds `baseDir` with no lock (T1). Then `writeProcessIdentity(record)` runs, still with no lock and no second claim check (T2). That write does `fs.mkdir(dirname, {recursive:true})`. If `cleanupIsolation` renames `baseDir` to `.retiring-*` in between, the write creates `baseDir/.omp-isolation-unfinished/<pid>.json` at the old path. That directory has no marker, so `clear` keeps it ("no owner marker"). Meanwhile the writer's real directory is being deleted.

Normally the writer's lease holds teardown off during that window. The one lease teardown ignores is the owner's own child session (`isOwnersOwnLease`), so the window is reachable only on that path. I did not build a probe that pauses between T1 and T2. The fix would be to take the sandbox lock and check the claim again before writing, as `leaseIsolationWorkspace` already does.

The probe files are in the scratch directory, next to a `node_modules` symlink I added there so the probes can import the package; nothing was written inside the snapshot.
